what: The ideas register: the core ideas the second edition is made of, one node each, with where each came from (provenance), which 2018 chapters it answers, which proposed chapter it goes to, and its state. Authored by the librarian on 18 October 2026 from the nine co-written articles, the seven decisions, the newsroom survey and the 49 articles it brings, and the six briefs; extended whenever a new article is processed. A state is 'candidate' until Dinis accepts it (read, comment, decide); 'accepted' here means Dinis said it in a co-written article as his own position, and the decision on the text is still to be recorded in the vault by the editor.

kinds.frame: a way of seeing the whole book uses
kinds.claim: something the book asserts and must back
kinds.method: a way of working the reader can copy
kinds.evidence: a number or a source the book cites
kinds.process: how the book itself is made; the last part, or not the book at all

destinations.this-edition: in the second edition's first release
destinations.next-version: after the first release of the second edition
destinations.the-process: about how the book is made: the site, the workflow, not the reader's text

states.accepted: Dinis said it, in an article or a memo; to record in the vault as a decision on the text
states.drafting: the editor is writing it in the vault
states.declined: not doing it, with the reason
states.deferred: later, to a named version or book

ideas.title: The brief is the unit of work, and writing it as an article forces the research

ideas.title: Omnichannel programming: brief by voice, review on the phone, one shared state
ideas.statement: Voice, chat, phone, IDE and pull requests all read and write one shared state (git, vaults, briefs, graphs); this is how a new generation programs.

ideas.title: Every mistake added a rule: the complexity trap of the agent operator
ideas.statement: Each mistake becomes a rule, the prompt grows, compaction comes sooner and new mistakes follow; the way out is fewer, enforced rules, re-anchored after every summary.

ideas.title: Why your agents should not run on your laptop
ideas.statement: An agent on your laptop runs as you, with your SSH keys, cookies and password-manager session; pick the cloud surface by reach.

ideas.title: Direction is the scarce skill: the place of highest leverage
ideas.statement: When anyone can brief an agent, building stops being the bottleneck; choosing what to build next, where nothing blocks you, and starting without knowing the end, is what employers and users pay for.

ideas.title: Knowing when to stop is most of seniority
ideas.statement: Who the attackers are, the phase of the business, the bottleneck, what good enough looks like: experience gives people this, agents lack it, and the book has to teach the junior's version.

sources.where: the chapter on how the brain decides

ideas.title: One-way and two-way doors, blast radius, and where a person belongs
ideas.statement: How cheap is it to undo decides where the human goes: put the person where the output cannot be undone and the blast radius is large; give them the why; let the record move the line over time. People approve 93% of permission prompts.

ideas.title: Agents decide, people answer
ideas.statement: Agents in loops make real decisions, but responsibility stays with whoever granted the reach and set the mandate; also ELIZA and anthropomorphism.

ideas.title: Make fact-based decisions: think out loud and let the record check you
ideas.statement: Count rather than remember; publish only what the record supports (5 claims confirmed, 5 corrected, 2 not found); review as a record with every finding answered; distrust self-reports.

ideas.title: Mandate, reach and the gap: hope versus enforcement
ideas.statement: Before you give an agent access, write down what it is for and what it can reach; the gap is the risk; rules in a prompt are hope, rules in a hook or platform are enforcement; behaviour, decision and workflow policies are different things.

ideas.title: Code is a liability; the future is the smallest code that does the job
ideas.statement: Every shipped line is a capability someone may misuse (Log4j; 428 of 1,500 files ran); the next maintainer is an agent; the minimal viable code path.

ideas.title: Learning to hack is still how you learn how things work: draw the line where the attacker is
